# MouseOS

> MouseOS turns an Android phone into a wireless trackpad, air mouse, keyboard, media remote and presentation clicker for a Mac, a Windows PC or a Linux computer — and into a remote for Samsung, LG and Google TVs. It is free, works over the local Wi‑Fi with no internet connection, and has no account, no cloud, no ads and no tracking. Website: https://mouseos.app/

## Facts

- Name: MouseOS (on Google Play: "MouseOS — Mac, PC & TV Remote")
- Price: free, no ads. An optional tip can be left in the app's Settings.
- Phone app: Android 8 or later. In closed beta on Google Play: join at https://mouseos.app/#beta with a Google account email, get added to the test, install from Google Play. iPhone: on the way.
- Computer app (free, required for computers, not for TVs): macOS 11 or later on Apple silicon (.dmg), Windows 10 and 11 64‑bit (.msi), Linux 64‑bit on X11 or Wayland (.deb for Ubuntu/Debian/Mint, .rpm for Fedora/openSUSE). Downloads: https://github.com/MathisZerbib/mouseos/releases/latest
- TVs: Samsung, LG and Google TV (Sony, TCL, Philips…), controlled straight from the phone over the same Wi‑Fi.
- The six screens: PAD (trackpad: tap to click, two‑finger scroll or scroll strip, hold to drag), AIR (air mouse: aim the phone like a TV remote, gyroscope), REMOTE (arrows, play/pause, the computer's volume, next episode), TV, KEYS (keyboard in any language, accents and emoji), SLIDES (presentation clicker: giant next/previous, a timer, the volume buttons click).
- Connection: the phone and the computer talk directly over the local Wi‑Fi network, or over the phone's hotspot. No internet, no server, no account. The computer finds the phone by itself; each new phone is approved once with one ALLOW click on the computer.
- Privacy: no account, no cloud, no analytics, no advertising SDK. Nothing leaves your network. Policy: https://mouseos.app/privacy-policy.html
- Version: 2.0 (October 2026).
- Developer: Mathis Zerbib, independent. Contact: support@mouseos.app

## Setup in short

1. On the computer: install the free MouseOS companion app and allow it to control the pointer (macOS: Privacy & Security → Accessibility; Linux on Wayland: click ALLOW CONTROL; Windows: allow network access on a Private network).
2. On the phone: open MouseOS on the same Wi‑Fi. It finds the computer by itself.
3. On the computer: click ALLOW once for that phone. Done.

- [Phone as a presentation clicker](https://mouseos.app/presentation-remote.html): Keynote, PowerPoint, Google Slides; volume buttons turn slides, a timer that buzzes
- [Phone as a TV remote](https://mouseos.app/tv-remote.html): Samsung, LG and Google TV over Wi‑Fi, pairing for each
- [Linux, X11 and Wayland](https://mouseos.app/linux-remote-mouse.html): how input works on each session (XTest, uinput), ports, packages
- [MouseOS and other remote apps](https://mouseos.app/alternatives.html): what it does differently from Unified Remote, Remote Mouse and KDE Connect, and when they fit better
- [Privacy policy](https://mouseos.app/privacy-policy.html)
- [Downloads and README on GitHub](https://github.com/MathisZerbib/mouseos)
